A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, Figures 1–10, Algorithms 1–4, and Appendices A–I. The complete material supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original optimizer-convergence experiments on Gaussian, Generalized Rademacher, and shifted-diagonal data, including batch-size and momentum sweeps in Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original synthetic-data experiments and sensitivity results in Figures 1–10, with experimental settings in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4 and the AdamProxy update in Equation (4) retain the same procedures and objectives. The new Mahalanobis-norm terminology describes the existing mathematical formulation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Gaussian, structured Rademacher, and shifted-diagonal datasets and classification scenarios. Generalized Rademacher is renamed Scaled Rademacher, with its definition and experimental vectors unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding figures retain the same experiment-specific comparators: GD, full-batch Adam, stochastic and incremental Adam variants, AdamProxy, and full-batch/incremental Signum. The added related-work citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix C retains exponential loss, Gaussian data with N=10 and d=50, default Adam parameters (0.9, 0.95), Signum momentum 0.99, and the same learning-rate schedules. Cosine-similarity evaluation, parameter sweeps, and fixed-point stopping criteria also match.

E4.justification: The batch-size and momentum sensitivity studies in Figures 6–10 and Appendices A–B are retained unchanged. The structured-data and shifted-diagonal case studies were already present in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bands. The reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 1–10 retain identical plotted content and findings. Appendix C still reports fixed-point convergence within 20 iterations. Revised captions and terminology introduce no new outcomes or numerical corrections.

T1.justification: Appendix F.2 corrects the proof of Proposition 4.3: v1 infers gradient convergence directly from weighted summability, whereas v3 establishes a zero liminf and then uses monotonic loss to conclude convergence. The theorem conclusions remain unchanged. Corollary 3.2 shortens its assumption list, but separability remains incorporated through Definition 3.1.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows its novelty statement from first evidence that mini-batching alters Adam’s bias to a data-dependent characterization for batch size 1. The abstract also drops the near-one momentum qualification for Signum, although the introduction and Theorem 5.1 retain it.

C2.justification: The explanations involving coordinate adaptivity and the Adam–SGD gap are retained. Both versions discuss the same restrictions concerning beta2 approaching one, per-sample incremental updates, other sampling schemes, and the missing convergence guarantee for fixed-point iteration.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the same data-generation information, hyperparameters, use of CVXPY, uniform fixed-point initialization, and 10^-8 stopping threshold. The added reproducibility statement points to existing material without supplying new implementation details or resource-access information.

R1.justification: Sections 6–7 add Orvieto and Gower (2025), Zhang et al. (2025), Tsilivis et al. (2025), Vasudeva et al. (2025), and Marek et al. (2025). These modestly expand context on momentum, rotations, neural-network implicit bias, and small-batch language-model training.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites the abstract, introduction, notation, and limitations; renames GR data to SR data; and standardizes appendix references. Reproducibility and LLM-usage statements are added, while the section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The manuscript adopts ICLR formatting throughout, changing typography, text and figure widths, heading styles, title/author blocks, and running headers. Equations and floats are reflowed, including moving Figure 1 from the bottom to the top of page 2. The ten figures retain their internal plots, axes, and legends.

improvement.justification: v3 repairs a specific logical gap in Proposition 4.3’s proof and clarifies the contribution framing while adding relevant research context. The scientific scope and empirical support remain unchanged. The abstract’s omission of Signum’s momentum condition reduces precision, although the main text preserves it. Overall, the proof correction and clearer positioning provide a limited net improvement.
